seo.h1: Kalshi Alternatives 2026: Best Platforms by Use Case
seo.meta_description: Nine states still can't access all of Kalshi's sports contracts. Here's where to go instead, broken down by fees, availability, crypto funding, and use case.

summary: Nine states still can't access all of Kalshi's sports contracts, and the list keeps shifting as lawsuits move. This breaks down the real alternatives — Polymarket, Novig, ProphetX, FanDuel Predicts, Crypto.com, OG.com — by fees, availability, and what each one actually does better.
quick_answer: The best Kalshi alternative depends on why you're leaving: Polymarket is the closest Kalshi-style exchange for US traders, Novig has the lowest sports trading fees, ProphetX suits peer-to-peer parlay traders, and Crypto.com or Gemini Predictions work best for crypto-funded accounts. Availability varies by state, so check before assuming any of them are open where you live.

body.content: The most common reason is geography. There are currently nine states where Kalshi is unavailable and/or limited, with sports trading prohibited outright in Michigan, Nevada, and Ohio. Other trackers put the number closer to five or eight depending on how recently the litigation moved. Massachusetts sued Kalshi directly, and in January 2026 won a preliminary injunction blocking the company from offering sports contracts there unless it complies with the state's sports gaming law. Arizona's case went the other direction: the state filed criminal charges against Kalshi, but a federal judge later paused the case and temporarily blocked the state from enforcing its gambling laws against the company.

Availability varies by jurisdiction, and the fact that a platform showed up in a search last week doesn't mean it's cleared for your address this week. The second reason is fees — taker and maker spreads differ meaningfully across platforms, and the gap compounds on anyone trading more than a handful of contracts a month. The third reason is market mix: Kalshi leans toward economic data, elections, and culture tickers, while sports liquidity, peer-to-peer pricing, or crypto-funded accounts are often better served elsewhere.

content: US traders wanting the closest Kalshi-style exchange: Polymarket, which built the largest prediction market internationally and returned to the US through CFTC-regulated Polymarket US, launched December 2025
Sports-first trading: Novig, offering zero-fee pregame trades and live in-game markets
Parlay-style sports contracts: ProphetX, a peer-to-peer exchange built around custom parlays
Sportsbook-familiar interface: FanDuel Predicts, best for beginners coming from a traditional sportsbook background
Crypto-native funding: Crypto.com or Gemini Predictions, brokerage-style accounts with crypto deposit rails
Niche or social-flavored markets: OG.com, with a friendly user experience and strong social integration

body.content: None of these are a straight upgrade on Kalshi in every category. Polymarket wins on liquidity and brand recognition, Novig wins on fee structure for sports traders, and OG wins on vibe over volume. Pick by the column that matters to you, not by whichever name shows up first in a search result.

Prices on live markets move by the minute, so here's how the structural costs compare on a tested fee table: Polymarket charges up to $1.50 per 100 contracts, Novig up to $0.75, ProphetX up to $1.00, OG.com up to $1.75 (plus $1.99 bank withdrawals), FanDuel Predicts up to $2.00, and Crypto.com up to $1.75 (plus $1.99 bank withdrawals). None of them charge a maker fee.

On a $1 position, these differences barely register. On a few hundred dollars spread across a season of markets, the spread between Novig's roughly seventy-five cent fee and FanDuel Predicts' two-dollar fee on the same 100-lot size adds up fast. Treat any specific payout you see quoted anywhere, including on this site, as a snapshot, not a promise.

Kalshi and Polymarket both offer charting/order-book tools and API access alongside mobile apps. Novig and ProphetX have apps with limited desktop tools and no API. FanDuel Predicts and OG.com are mobile-first with no desktop tools or API. All six let you browse markets without an account. Apps that feature limit orders include Kalshi, Polymarket, Novig, ProphetX, and Crypto.com — if order-type control matters to how you trade, that shortens the list considerably before you even get to fees.
how to pick your kalshi alternative

content: Are you in a state where Kalshi's sports contracts are currently restricted or disputed? Check availability before assuming any named alternative is cleared for you either — several states have active lawsuits against more than one platform at once
Do you want to fund with crypto, or strictly fiat? Crypto.com and Gemini Predictions lean crypto-forward; Polymarket, Novig, and FanDuel Predicts are fiat-first for US accounts
Are you chasing longshot payouts or hedging a position you already hold? Peer-to-peer exchanges like ProphetX let you set your own price
Do you need an API or desktop charting, or are you trading from a phone during a game? That alone rules out two or three names from the table

faqs.q: What is the best Kalshi alternative for sports trading?
faqs.a: Novig, for its zero-fee pregame trades and live in-game markets, with ProphetX as a peer-to-peer option for custom parlays.

faqs.q: Is Polymarket a good Kalshi alternative in the US?
faqs.a: Yes — Polymarket US launched in December 2025 as a separate CFTC-regulated exchange, making it the closest Kalshi-style option for US traders in terms of liquidity and brand recognition.

faqs.q: Which Kalshi alternative has the lowest fees?
faqs.a: Novig, at up to $0.75 per 100 contracts, compared to FanDuel Predicts at up to $2.00 for the same size.

faqs.q: Which Kalshi alternatives support crypto funding?
faqs.a: Crypto.com and Gemini Predictions are the crypto-forward options, offering brokerage-style accounts with crypto deposit rails alongside event contracts.
